critic_notes.rationale: The construction is internally consistent and the EV algebra is correct, but a SUMRANK average of the published enterprise-multiple (EBITDA/EV) anomaly and the published asset/capacity-growth anomaly is an additive blend of two known effects with no genuine interaction, so any result is hard to attribute to the cross-theme premise.

This is essentially the product of the two FF5 factor legs themselves (HML and CMA), so it is both a rediscovery of documented value and investment effects and largely self-defeating under an FF5 alpha benchmark that will absorb the very exposures the signal is built from.

The state-dependent framing is a legitimately different structure from the usual additive value+investment blend, but the multiplicative 0/1 gate collapses every non-decelerating firm — cheap and expensive alike — into an identical bottom bucket, so the short leg tests nothing about valuation and the spread partly measures capex deceleration alone.

A rank difference between the published sales-to-price ratio and a PP&E-plus-inventory growth measure (itself close to the documented asset-growth and inventory-growth anomalies) is again a purely additive pairing of known effects, and it duplicates the mechanism of the first proposal with a cosmetically different valuation leg.

The overvaluation-times-external-deployment interaction is economically coherent, sign-consistent with the expression, and the COALESCE convention is defensible; the main caveat is proximity to the documented net-issuance and stock-financed-acquirer literatures, so the value added must come from the joint conditioning rather than either leg.

Three-year-smoothed free-cash-flow yield is a standard, widely published valuation ratio rather than a cross-theme interaction — subtracting capex inside the numerator is simply the definition of FCF, not an investment-discipline conditioning — and oancf availability will additionally truncate the sample.

The INDICATOR→SIGN swap is a substantive repair rather than cosmetics — it converts a degenerate one-sided gate (which produced no computable long-short stats) into a two-sided spread that actively shorts cheap-but-accelerating firms — though it remains a close descendant of the archived gen-0 signal and its short leg is deep-value stocks, which may fight the FF5 value factor.

This is a conjunctive value × asset-growth double sort, i.e. essentially the classic B/M and asset-growth anomalies combined, and the claim that MIN "cannot be replicated by any linear mix of HML and CMA loadings" confuses a nonlinear construction rule with factor exposure — the resulting portfolio will load heavily on both HML and CMA regardless.

With dvc typically an order of magnitude smaller than capx for most firms, this ratio is dominated by −(capx+aqc)/market cap, making it a near-rediscovery of the capital-investment-to-price anomaly dressed as a payout measure, and the "not a free-cash-flow yield" defense concedes it omits the one term (operating cash flow) that would make the allocation story economically well-posed.

Incremental EBITDA per dollar of lagged capex is a genuinely different construct from investment level or growth — it is a marginal-productivity measure rather than a quantity — the sign logic and the winsorized small-denominator handling are internally consistent, and the value leg's role as a conditioner is economically coherent rather than a repackaged quality-times-value composite.

The economic mechanism is the same rich-valuation-plus-empire-building story as the archived Expensive_Externally_Funded_Empire (which already delivered strong FMB but a weak, wrong-signed portfolio spread), and the proposal swaps both legs without diagnosing why that FMB/alpha divergence occurred; separately, COALESCE(gdwl,0) inside DELTA will manufacture spurious first-time-reporting jumps.

Replacing the investment level with capex acceleration is a defensible refinement that shifts the signal from chronically capital-intensive firms to the turn in spending, and the diagnosis of which gen-0 signal was sign-consistent is accurate, but a second difference of an annual ratio is noisy and will cost coverage, so the gain over the parent signal is uncertain.

The expression is internally coherent and the sign logic of the two-sided SIGN gate is correct, but it is a bundled double-tweak (RANK→IND_RANK, capx→capx+aqc) of the archived Signed_Capex_Discipline_Gated_Earnings_Yield that confounds attribution and risks reproducing the parent's near-zero alpha rather than diagnosing why the gated earnings yield failed to survive FF5.

A second-moment notion of capital-allocation discipline is genuinely distinct from the level/change/acceleration constructions already archived and is not spanned by CMA, though the volatility leg is mechanically small for asset-light or near-zero-capex firms, so the spread should be checked for a size/asset-lightness tilt rather than a true stability effect.

This is another leg-swap of the archived Own_History_Peak_Valuation_And_Investment (P/B→P/S, capx→capx+aqc) whose parent already had marginal, sign-inconsistent portfolio evidence, and TS_RANK over five annual observations is too coarse to give the "self-timing" construct much resolution.

The human-capital investment channel is untested in this archive and the sign logic is consistent, but the hiring-rate leg is a well-known published anomaly (Bazdresch–Belo–Lin employee growth), so the proposal's value hinges entirely on the interaction with market value per employee, and `emp` is a stale, sparsely reported field that will likely depress coverage.

Inventory growth in excess of sales growth is verbatim one of the Lev–Thiagarajan/Abarbanell–Bushee fundamental signals with the same predicted negative sign, so the reasoning's claim that this leg is "distinguishable from known anomalies" is simply wrong and the signal is largely a known anomaly scaled by a conventional price-to-sales rank.

This is an industry z-score wrapper applied to an archived signal with no change to the mechanism — the definition of a cosmetic variant — and it is also not a cross-theme interaction at all, while the near-zero/negative TS_SUM(capx,5) denominator remains an unaddressed source of the very asset-lightness sorting it claims to fix.

A clean single-variable ablation of the archive's best-performing gate structure with a coherent distributable-liquidity story and sign-consistent construction, though the net-cash-to-price leg overlaps substantially with the known net-leverage/net-debt-to-price effect, so any gain must be shown to come from the interaction rather than the leverage tilt.

Converting the discrete one-year funding gate into a five-year persistence score is a substantive (not cosmetic) upgrade that directly addresses turnover and transitory-capex-pause contamination while preserving the two-sided sign structure that produced the archive's only clean alpha.

Replacing SIGN with RANK destroys the two-sided structure the hypothesis relies on — the product becomes strictly non-negative, so the short leg is no longer cash-rich burners but low-cash low-surplus firms — and what remains is close to the already-tested Cheapness_Times_Self_Funded_Surplus with only cosmetic substitutions (ceq→che, oancf→ebitda) that previously delivered the wrong sign.

A well-posed attribution test that holds the funding-state gate fixed while swapping the valuation leg, and is distinct from the archived capex-deceleration-gated earnings yield, giving an interpretable read on whether the alpha comes from the gate or the cash-to-price channel.

The mechanism swap is legitimate and the choice of gross rather than net PP&E is well reasoned, but gross PP&E declines for only a small minority of firms, so the gate will be badly unbalanced (a thin, likely distress-tilted long leg) and the signal risks collapsing into an interacted asset-growth/investment anomaly.

This is essentially a free-cash-flow/cash-flow-to-price yield with a cash-to-price term added — both long-published value anomalies — and the stated defense fails because adding a balance-sheet stock to an annual flow in one numerator is dimensionally incoherent and makes the ratio's units scale-dependent rather than genuinely cross-theme.

This is a mechanical fusion of two archived designs (magnitude coverage from Cash_Value_Times_Internal_Funding_Coverage plus the multi-year smoothing of Cash_Value_Times_Chronic_Self_Funding) rather than a new mechanism, and averaging a winsorized ratio whose denominator can approach zero leaves the un-ranked second leg's scale, not its economics, driving the spread.

The switch from an industry-z-scored skewed level to a within-firm directional gate is a defensible repair and the hypothesis matches the expression's sign, but the gate is partly mechanically redundant with the cash-to-price leg (a rising runway is largely rising cash) and the che/(capx+aqc) ratio's near-zero denominators make its three-year mean unstable.

This is a clean, well-identified ablation that strips profitability out of the winning gate to test whether the archived alpha is investment restraint or an RMW-flavoured tilt, the gate is genuinely two-sided at an economically meaningful reference point, and the sign logic is internally consistent.

The external-finance-dependence gate is a new channel for this archive but leans on the well-documented net-external-financing/composite-issuance anomaly, and the claim that it is "two-sided" is weak since ebitda exceeds new equity plus debt issuance for the large majority of firms, so the short leg will be small and tilted toward unprofitable microcaps.

SIGN(GROWTH(revt)−GROWTH(ppegt)) is essentially the same state variable as the archive's GROWTH(sale/ppegt), which already delivered a significantly wrong-signed FF5 alpha (−3.9%, t=−3.08) under the same positive prior, so the proposal re-tests a direction the archive has already contradicted without addressing why.

Swapping RANK for IND_RANK on one leg of the archive's best signal is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against; it is a robustness check rather than a new economic hypothesis and should be run as a diagnostic on the existing signal, not proposed as a distinct candidate.

A clean, well-specified one-leg ablation of the archive's best signal (organic-vs-acquisitive deployment) that isolates whether the valuation channel must be the unvalued cash hoard, though as a pure attribution swap it is unlikely to improve on the gen-4 result and risks being read as a cosmetic variant if it merely reproduces it.

The serial-acquirer framing gives the three-year smoothing genuine economic content and the bounded term avoids the denominator instability that plagues averaged coverage ratios, but it remains an incremental smoothing of the gen-4 winner and inherits the undefined-when-capx+aqc≈0 problem for asset-light firms.

The bounded three-destination reformulation is a legitimate test of whether the effect is anti-acquisition or pro-owner, but it sits in mild tension with the archive's own payout-for-capex-substitution logic by pooling dividends and capex as jointly "good," so a null result will be hard to attribute cleanly between the two channels.

Moving from the acquisition flow to the industry-adjusted goodwill stock is a substantively different, slower-moving state variable with a coherent impairment-risk mechanism, though goodwill intensity is close to a published intangible/impairment anomaly and COALESCE(gdwl,0) will lump genuine non-reporters with true zero-goodwill firms.

Netting a single year's acquisition outlay from the cash stock is a small perturbation of plain cash-to-price — a well-known published anomaly — and it abandons the cross-theme interaction structure entirely while the claimed dimensional coherence still subtracts an annual flow from a balance-sheet stock.

The conjunctive MIN is a genuinely different combination rule from the additive/multiplicative forms already tested and both validated states share an economic zero, but the two inputs have very different scales and upper ranges, so the MIN will mechanically be dominated by the bounded composition term for most healthy firms and the "weakest test" interpretation is weaker than claimed.

Because MIN(SIGN, ratio) already equals the ratio whenever the funding test passes and a constant when it fails, the ADD version produces the identical cross-sectional ordering except within the failing (short) group, making this much closer to an aggregation tweak of the archived Weakest_Discipline_Test than the "orthogonal cells" framing claims, and the stated rationale about incomparable ranges is factually wrong since both legs are already bounded in [-1,1].

This is a genuine information-adding refinement of the archive's strongest signal — it preserves the economic zero of the earned-versus-raised comparison while re-ordering firms within each side by intensity, and the |internal|+|external| denominator is a defensible bounded normalization (worth checking behavior when EBITDA is negative and external flows are negative, where the sign convention is economically ambiguous).

The multi-year cumulation of the sources test is economically sensible and distinct from the archived uses-side persistence signal, but taking SIGN of the three-year sums discards exactly the "fraction of years" gradation that made chronic self-funding work (an MA of annual signs would be the better test), and the supporting reasoning misreports a drop in fmb_tstat from 4.27 to 3.98 as a gain.

Replacing the sparse, non-monotone goodwill stock with five-year cumulative acquisition cash flow is a correctly diagnosed repair that should restore coverage and a true zero point while retaining the slow-moving deal-history concept; the main risk is that an un-winsorized IND_ZSCORE of a heavily zero-inflated, right-skewed variable lets a few mega-acquirers dominate the spread.

The dominant leg is negative share-count growth, i.e. the well-published net share issuance anomaly, and since acquisition-financed issuance shows up in csho growth the two terms partially double-count the same event while being on non-comparable scales (a growth rate minus an assets-scaled outlay), so the signal likely just reloads a known anomaly interacted with cash-to-price.

Scaling both outlay legs by market cap makes the second factor mechanically correlated with the RANK(cash/price) leg through the shared price denominator, so the construct largely squares a valuation tilt (and its capx/price term is itself the known investment-to-price anomaly) rather than isolating the deal-scale mechanism the hypothesis describes.

The expression matches the hypothesis and both legs are correctly bounded on a common [−1,+1] scale with a shared economic zero, but it is only an equal-weight sum of two already-archived second legs, so the likely outcome is an intermediate blend rather than new information — its value rests entirely on the paired comparison with the MIN version.

The self-financing gate already exists in the archive in three forms (one-year sign, three-year-sum sign, and continuous intensity), and MA(SIGN,·) versus SIGN(TS_SUM,·) is a cosmetic smoothing variant of the same construct that is near-certain to be highly correlated with the existing 4.6–4.9 t-stat results without testing a new economic claim.

The dollar-weighted five-year mix is a defensible fix to the zero-inflated, skewed industry z-score of cumulative deal spend and is internally consistent, but it will be heavily collinear with the archived three-year moving-average mix (alpha 4.4%, t 4.15), so any gain is likely marginal rather than mechanistic.

The diagnosis is correct — the earlier MIN paired a winsorized-but-unbounded coverage ratio with a bounded mix, so the minimum was decided by scale rather than by economics — and placing both legs on a common bounded scale makes the conjunction claim genuinely testable against the additive form, though the incremental economic content over the two standalone legs remains modest.

This is the only proposal opening a genuinely untested (short-horizon, reversible) investment dimension and its sign convention is coherent, but the second leg is close to the published inventory-growth anomaly (Thomas–Zhang) and the COALESCE(invt,0) convention forces all inventory-free firms to an exact zero that sits in the middle of the second leg's distribution, contaminating the interaction with a large, economically heterogeneous mass point.
